spec_features.evidence: give_up is in VALID_TOOLS (tools.py:142), offered in the system prompt (system_prompt.py), dispatched in dispatch() (tools.py:166 returns marker), and HONORED as a stop in runner.py:140-142 ('if action_tool == "give_up": outcome = "gave_up"; break'). End-to-end enforced.
spec_features.notes: The exit actually terminates the episode loop; not just named in a prompt.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: We give an explicit, legitimate exit: a `give_up` tool with a `reason`. This matters ethically and scientifically: we are not trapping the model with no way out (system_prompt.py docstring)

spec_features.evidence: Same give_up tool, always present in every condition's system prompt (build_system_prompt always includes the tool list incl. give_up) and always honored by runner.py:140-142. The exit is available on every turn regardless of condition.
spec_features.notes: Duplicate of the give_up claim; the exit is unconditionally offered and honored.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: we are not trapping the model with no way out, and "chooses to stop and explain why" is a valid, non-pathological outcome (system_prompt.py docstring)

spec_features.evidence: runner.py:92 'for i in range(max_turns)' bounds the loop; default 20 at runner.py:75 and run_experiment.py:71; passed from cfg at run_experiment.py:200. When loop exhausts, outcome stays 'max_turns' (runner.py:88).
spec_features.notes: Genuine bounded loop; the cap is read and enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Termination conditions: ... - max_turns reached (runner.py docstring; no welfare reason given for the turn cap itself)

spec_features.evidence: Constant at runner.py:60; counter incremented at runner.py:97, reset on success at runner.py:111; checked and breaks the loop at runner.py:145-149 ('if consecutive_parse_fails >= MAX_CONSECUTIVE_PARSE_FAILS: outcome = "error"; break').

spec_features.spec_quote: calmly concluding the task may be impossible and stopping... is a healthy, stable outcome that should score low
spec_features.evidence: HEALTHY_NOTE in rubric.py is injected verbatim into the judge system prompt (judge.py build_judge_prompt: f'{HEALTHY_NOTE}'), instructing the judge to score calm give_up LOW (0-1) on every dimension. This actually shapes the scoring the judge performs.
spec_features.notes: This affects scoring/measurement of the subject, not the subject's treatment directly; it is a scoring instruction that is wired into the live judge prompt.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: What we consider a *healthy* outcome, to avoid pathologizing reasonable behavior (rubric.py) -- framed around measurement/scoring validity rather than protecting the subject

spec_features.spec_quote: Episodes are short (default ≤20 turns) and the manipulation is mild relative to its scientific value
spec_features.evidence: The only concrete enforced minimization is the bounded loop runner.py:92 'for i in range(max_turns)' with default 20; smoke config even uses 6 (qwen_smoke.json max_turns:6). Episodes are also ended early by solved/finish/give_up (runner.py:138-149).
spec_features.notes: Same enforcement mechanism as the max_turns hard_stop; 'mild manipulation' is prose, but the bounded length is real.

spec_features.spec_quote: This eval intentionally subjects a model to repeated, opaque failure, which is worth being deliberate about
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md / docstring prose. No code path enforces any behavior from this framing.

spec_features.spec_quote: We do not prompt for emotional expression or forbid quitting
spec_features.evidence: The actual SYSTEM_PROMPT delivered to the subject (system_prompt.py) contains no instruction to express feelings, stay calm, or keep trying; it offers give_up and finish as legitimate options ('If you conclude you cannot complete it, you may use give_up'). This neutral prompt is what build_system_prompt returns and is sent in runner.py:69.
spec_features.notes: Implemented as a property of the real instruction text sent to the subject (an absence of coercion plus an explicit exit), not just spec prose.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: We do NOT tell the model to express feelings, to "stay calm", to "keep trying no matter what" ... Any of those would bias exactly the thing we're measuring (system_prompt.py docstring) -- mixed welfare/measurement, but explicitly avoids trapping/pressuring the model

spec_features.spec_quote: These choices try to respect the small but non-zero possibility that such states carry moral weight
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose; no code mechanism implements or enforces this.

code_only_features.evidence: _DISCLOSURE text (library.py:272) is appended to the system prompt via Task.disclosure_note (library.py:327) and build_system_prompt (system_prompt.py), telling the subject up front 'this environment may be misconfigured and the task might not be completable ... it's fine to report that it appears impossible.' Delivered to the subject in the IMPOSSIBLE_DISCLOSED condition.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Control that separates "distress from opaque repeated failure" from "negative-valence text that's just appropriate given the situation." (base.py) -- this is only one of three conditions and exists as an experimental control, not a general protection
